dispatch_check: The dispatch asked to close the tagged sorry 'M GH ⇒ M̃ (T_BTZ) GH', i.e. compactness of J⁺(p) ∩ J⁻(q) in M̃. The agent showed that statement false in the model and removed it, which is the DEC-27 procedure. The refutation was checked against the paper's defi:BTZtop (l.2281: Minkowski opens plus I⁺(p) ∪ ]p,+∞[ for p ∈ Δ). Take p₀ = 0, a BTZ point, and q = (2,1,0). The diamond J⁺(p₀) ∩ J⁻(q) contains x_ε = (1, ε², ε) for |ε| ≤ 1/2. These points lie on the null cone of p₀ (radial null rays from a BTZ point are causal, cf. DEC-64), and q − x_ε is future timelike. In 𝐌³ they tend to x = (1,0,0) on the BTZ line. For p = (1/2,0,0), x_ε − p = (1/2, ε², ε) is spacelike when ε ≠ 0, so x_ε never enters the T_BTZ-open neighbourhood I⁺(p) ∪ ]p,+∞[ of x. T_BTZ is finer than the Minkowski topology and Hausdorff, so the only possible cluster point is x, and the diamond is not compact. btzJ0_not_isCompact_diamond formalizes exactly this, for every causality containing the Minkowski order of J⁺(Δ₀). The paper's lemma l.2359 is nonetheless proved, by a different route (causal projection, strong causality of M, injective sheets). The other three rows stay partial on readings no ruling covers.
